text: These are the inheritances the Israelites received in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of Israel allotted to them.
Their inheritance was assigned by lot, as the LORD had commanded through Moses, for the nine and a half tribes.
For Moses had given the inheritance of the two and a half tribes beyond the Jordan, but to the Levites he gave no inheritance among them.

For the sons of Joseph had become two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim; and the Levites were given no share of the land, only towns to live in, with pasturelands for their livestock and their possessions.

versions.text: The sons of Joseph had become two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. The Levites were given no share of the land, only towns to live in, with pasturelands for their livestock and their possessions.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew כִּי links this verse explanatorily to verse 3 (why nine and a half tribes received land). Restoring the connective "For" preserves the logic of the passage and keeps the flow of the reading.

text: The Israelites did as the LORD had commanded Moses, and they divided the land.
Then the people of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him: "You know what the LORD said to Moses, the man of God, at Kadesh-barnea concerning you and me.
I was forty years old when Moses the servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh-barnea to scout out the land, and I brought him back a report just as I saw it in my heart.

versions.text: I was forty years old when Moses the servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh-barnea to scout out the land, and I brought him back an honest report.
versions.explanation: "An honest report" flattens the Hebrew idiom "as it was in my heart," which stresses Caleb's sincere conviction rather than mere factual accuracy.

text: My brothers who went up with me made the heart of the people melt, but I followed the LORD my God wholeheartedly.
On that day Moses swore this oath: 'The land where you have set your foot will surely be your inheritance and your children's forever, because you have followed the LORD my God wholeheartedly.'

And now, look: the LORD has kept me alive, just as he promised, these forty-five years since he spoke this word to Moses, while Israel journeyed through the wilderness. Here I am today, eighty-five years old.
I am still as strong today as I was the day Moses sent me out; my strength now is the same as it was then, for war and for going out and coming in.

So give me this hill country the LORD spoke of that day, for you yourself heard then that the Anakites are there, with large fortified cities. It may be that the LORD will be with me, and I will drive them out, just as the LORD said."

versions.text: So give me this hill country the LORD spoke of that day. You heard then that the Anakites are there, with large fortified cities. But if the LORD is with me, I will drive them out, just as the LORD said."
versions.explanation: אוּלַי expresses hopeful expectation ("perhaps / it may be that"), not a condition. "If" turns Caleb's confident hope into a conditional statement and slightly weakens the sense of trust in the LORD's promise.

versions.text: So give me this hill country the LORD spoke of that day. You heard then that the Anakites are there, with large fortified cities. It may be that the LORD will be with me, and I will drive them out, just as the LORD said."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has the causal particle כִּי plus the emphatic independent pronoun אַתָּה ("for you yourself heard"). Caleb is grounding his request in Joshua's own knowledge, and joining the clauses with "for" also reads more smoothly aloud than two flat sentences. The current rendering drops both the connective and the emphasis.

text: Then Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh and gave him Hebron as his inheritance.
So Hebron has belonged to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite as an inheritance to this day, because he followed the LORD, the God of Israel, wholeheartedly.
Hebron was formerly called Kiriath-arba, after the greatest man among the Anakites. And the land had rest from war.
